chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from a man, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the sun rises and with it are four Angels. One Angel calls out: 'O performer of the goodness, complete (it) and receive glad tidings!' And an Angel calls out: 'O performer of the evil, remove (it) and shorten (it)!' And an Angel calls out: 'Giving the expenses remains behind and withholding is damaging!' And an Angel sprinkles it (the earth) with the water, and had it not been for that, the ground would burst.
ai.seo_question: What is the role of the four Angels at sunrise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration links the daily cosmic order to moral accountability, where angels announce the spiritual status of humanity at dawn, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the tangible consequences of charity and stinginess. The text underscores the interplay between the physical world and divine mercy, noting that angelic intervention prevents the earth from scorching, thereby sustaining life for human worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that natural phenomena are not merely mechanical but are imbued with theological significance and divine sustenance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from a man, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The sun emerges and with it are four Angels. One Angel calls out: ‘O performer of the goodness, complete (it) and receive glad tidings!’ And an Angel calls out: ‘O performer of the evil, remove (it) and shorten (it)!’ And an Angel calls out: ‘Giving the expenses remains behind and withholding is damaging!’ And an Angel sprinkles it (the earth) with the water, and had it not been for that, the ground would burst’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid all from al- Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from a man from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when the sun rises, there are four angels with it. One angel calls, ‘O people of good deeds, complete your good deeds and for you there is glad news.’ Another angel calls, ‘O people of evil deeds, you must stop and stay away from evil deeds.’ The other angel says, To spend for deserving causes is a saving, and to withhold such spending is a sure loss.’ One angel keeps throwing water on it; otherwise, the earth catches fire.”
